svg.title: Option A and option B on the reproduction state
svg.desc: Left: option A, the stall search treats AGV-1 as an illegal pose, skips P15 and stashes T27 on W31. Right: option B, AGV-1 moves to the free charger C10 first and T27 is parked on P15.

g.text: Option A: skip the stall that overlaps an AGV

g.text: AGV-1 stays on C14 and keeps charging.

g.text: P15 is rejected as a destination; no other stall is

text.font-family: 'IBM Plex Sans', 'Segoe UI', Roboto, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

g.text: free, so tier 2 stashes T27 on waypoint W31.

g.text: Map labels: P17, W22, B21, C14 = node_id 17, 22, 21, 14 (P parking, W waypoint, B bay, C AGV charger); T17 = tray_id 17; AGV-1 = agv_id 1; X@90 = GaragePose {node_id: X, heading: 90}, heading in degrees [-179, 180],

g.text: Two ways out: avoid the stall, or clear it

text.font-family: 'IBM Plex Sans', 'Segoe UI', Roboto, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

g.text: Both start from the detection that option A adds: the stall search must know which stalls a parked AGV overlaps. Option A then looks elsewhere; option B spends one AGV move to use the

text.font-family: 'IBM Plex Sans', 'Segoe UI', Roboto, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

g.text: best stall. Routes are graph walks for illustration, not recorded plans.
